report:
## Conclusion

The claim is well supported: the adjuvanted recombinant zoster vaccine (RZV, Shingrix) substantially reduces the risk of herpes zoster (shingles) in adults aged 70 and older, with efficacy that appears durable over roughly a decade.

## Evidence

**Randomized controlled trial (ZOE-70):** The pivotal Phase 3 trial specifically enrolling adults ≥70 years (Cunningham et al., NEJM 2016) found RZV reduced herpes zoster incidence by 89.8% (95% CI, 84.2–93.7) compared with placebo. Combined analysis with the ZOE-50 trial (which also included participants ≥70) showed pooled efficacy of 91.3% in this age group, similar to efficacy in younger cohorts, indicating the vaccine remains highly effective even as immune senescence typically weakens vaccine responses (https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1603800).

**Systematic review (Cochrane):** The Cochrane review "Vaccines for preventing shingles in older adults" evaluated RZV alongside the live-attenuated vaccine and confirmed high-certainty evidence of RZV's strong protective effect against herpes zoster in adults 50+ and specifically in those 70+, based on pooled trial data (https://www.cochrane.org/CD008858/ARI_vaccines-preventing-shingles-older-adults).

**Long-term follow-up:** An extended follow-up study (ZOE-LTFU, published in eClinicalMedicine, 2025) found that efficacy remained high roughly 10–11 years after vaccination, supporting durability of protection in this older population (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/eclinm/article/PIIS2589-5370(25)00173-7/fulltext).

**Real-world effectiveness:** A large post-licensure effectiveness study published in Lancet Healthy Longevity corroborated trial results, showing RZV significantly reduced incident herpes zoster and postherpetic neuralgia in routine clinical practice, reinforcing that efficacy translates to real-world effectiveness (https://www.thelancet.com/journals/lanhl/article/PIIS2666-7568(22)00039-3/fulltext).

Together, randomized trial data, systematic review synthesis, long-term follow-up, and real-world effectiveness studies converge to strongly support the claim.
